agent_notes: No security vulnerabilities found in this diff. It is a pure HTML form-restructuring change in triggarr/templates/settings.html with no new string interpolation into SQL/exec/HTML sinks, no secrets, no CSRF impact (CSRF is handled by OriginCheckMiddleware in triggarr/__main__.py, independent of form structure), and no change to Jinja2 autoescaping (no `| safe` added).

Functional (non-security) regression worth flagging to the bugs/correctness reviewer: this diff reverts commit 542d5dd ('General settings fields lived in a separate form from the Save button, so saving never submitted them'). It re-wraps the General-section fields in their own <form> (settings.html lines 18-90) with no submit button, while the 'Save Settings' button remains in the separate apps/instances <form> (lines 134-246), both posting to the same save_settings endpoint. Because save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539) reads log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes, max_consecutive_failures, and skip_unreleased via form.get(...) with hardcoded fallbacks when absent, clicking 'Save Settings' will silently reset all General settings to defaults again. Not flagged as a security finding since the fallback values are safe (e.g. log_level defaults to 'info', not a verbose/debug mode) and no auth/secret fields are involved.

This finding is a user-facing functional regression and only falls under the architecture lane in part. The architecture caps limit pattern-consistency findings to medium. The bugs/impact lanes should rate the same site (settings.html:18 and :134) high or critical, because every Save destroys data in the user's config.

The deleted HTML comments explained why form= association is needed: the Security form (save_security, line 97) sits between General and the instances, and nested forms are illegal HTML. That constraint has not changed, so the reason for 542d5dd's design still applies.

Evidence I checked: `git log -1 --stat HEAD` (542d5dd changed this template and tests/test_web.py), the current template's form/button layout (only one 'Save Settings' button, at line 241, inside the second form), the save_settings handler's per-field defaults in routes.py, and the regression test's assertions.
No import cycles, new dependencies, duplication or layering problems: the change touches only a template.

Blast radius: one template, but the effect is persisted config. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:521-539) rebuilds `general` from form data with defaults instead of merging with current settings. Any POST that lacks the General fields therefore overwrites all 8 General values in the TOML, and the scheduler reloads with them.

Most visible user impact: skip_unreleased silently flips to False on every Save Settings click. log_level, hard_max_per_cycle, max_history_rows, request_timeout, page_size, tracking_window_minutes and max_consecutive_failures fall back to their handler defaults.

When a user clicks Save Settings, the POST has no General fields. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:530-539) then rebuilds the whole `general` block from `form.get(...)` with fallbacks and writes it to the TOML: log_level goes to the safe_log_level default, hard_max_per_cycle to 0, max_history_rows to 1000, request_timeout to 30, page_size to 50, tracking_window_minutes to 60, max_consecutive_failures to 5, and skip_unreleased to False (`form.get("skip_unreleased") == "on"`). Pressing Enter inside the General form does not submit it either: it has no submit button and holds several number inputs that block implicit submission, so the user cannot save General edits at all. Any instance edit also silently overwrites the operator's General config.
